units.title: The ROS 2 Graph
units.blurb: Nodes, topics, services and actions: how robot programs talk.

units.title: Units, Frames and Simulation
units.blurb: The shared conventions that let programs agree, and how simulators step time.

topics.title: Nodes and Topics
topics.short: Each job is a node; nodes publish and subscribe to named topics at steady rates.
topics.trouble: Students make one giant program, or forget that a topic with no publisher just stays silent.

topics.title: Services and Actions
topics.short: A topic streams, a service asks once and waits for one reply, and an action runs a long task with feedback and can be canceled.
topics.trouble: Students use a service for a long task, so the caller freezes until it is done.

topics.title: Units and Axes: REP 103
topics.short: ROS uses SI units (meters, seconds, radians) and right-handed frames: x forward, y left, z up.
topics.trouble: Students publish degrees or centimeters where every other node expects radians and meters.

topics.title: Chains of Transforms
topics.short: A point in the camera's frame reaches the map through a chain: camera to base, base to map.
topics.trouble: Students apply the transforms in the wrong order.

topics.title: How a Simulator Steps Time
topics.short: A simulator advances in fixed steps Δt; the real-time factor is simulated time over wall-clock time.
topics.trouble: Students think a slow simulation gives wrong answers, or that a large time step is always fine.
